title: New Pentagon files reveal 1953 sighting of dark, elliptical UFO
excerpt: Pentagon releases 43 UFO records, including a 1953 sighting, CIA documents, Project Blue Book files and military videos.
content:
Key Takeaways

  • Pentagon releases 43 records, including 40 documents and three military videos, in its eighth PURSUE tranche.

  • A 1953 report describes a dark, elliptical object spotted by Lockheed engineer Kelly Johnson and flight-test personnel in California.

  • The collection includes 1952 CIA documents, Project Blue Book records and intelligence files, with another release already in preparation.

The US Department of War has released a 1953 report detailing a dark, elongated elliptical object spotted by legendary Lockheed engineer Clarence “Kelly” Johnson and military flight-test personnel in California.

The account is part of the eighth tranche of previously classified and historical unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) records published on November 20 under the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters (PURSUE).

The report, identified as DOW-UAP-D206, compiles witness statements, sketches, and correspondence concerning a December 16, 1953, sighting near Agoura and Point Mugu in Southern California.

Johnson and other witnesses described an unusual dark object with an elongated, elliptical appearance. Personnel aboard a Lockheed WV-2 aircraft also reported observing the phenomenon while flying over the coast.

The Air Force’s Air Technical Intelligence Center (ATIC) eventually classified the sighting as a lenticular cloud. However, witness accounts questioned that explanation, describing the object’s apparent movement and sharply defined edges.

The report does not include radar data, photographs or physical evidence that could establish the object’s identity. Its release nevertheless provides a more complete historical record of an unusual observation involving experienced aerospace personnel.

Files span decades

The latest release contains 43 records, comprising 40 documents and three videos from the Department of War and the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA).

Among the historical material are six CIA documents from 1952 examining flying-saucer reports and their potential national security implications. Some discuss the possibility of convening a panel of scientists to assess available evidence.

The release also includes Air Force intelligence reports from 1957, several Project Blue Book case records, and documents concerning the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP) and its associated contractor work.

Three videos submitted by US Central Command also feature in the latest batch. The footage includes infrared sensor recordings from military platforms in the Middle East, with the cases remaining unresolved.

Another notable inclusion is a 2009 report prepared by Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS) under a Defense Intelligence Agency contract. The document discusses investigations into reported anomalous activity, including work associated with Utah’s Skinwalker Ranch.

More records to follow

The eighth release brings the total number of records published under PURSUE to 521, according to the program’s public archive.

President Donald Trump announced the initiative in February, directing the Department of War and other federal agencies to identify and release government records concerning extraterrestrial life, UFOs and UAP.

The first tranche appeared on May 8, with subsequent releases adding historical reports, military footage and intelligence documents.

The Department of War has confirmed that another batch of records is already in preparation. Assistant to the Secretary of War for Public Affairs and Pentagon Chief Spokesman Sean Parnell said the department and its agency partners were actively working on the next release.

“The Department of War and our agency partners are actively working on the next release of UAP files,” Parnell said in a statement.

The department said the eighth tranche would remain accessible through its official PURSUE archive at WAR.GOV/UFO, with additional documents to be published on a rolling basis. It did not specify when the next batch would be released or how many records it would contain.

The department describes the published materials as unresolved cases in which available evidence has not allowed officials to reach a definitive conclusion about the observed phenomena.
